findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 8 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: Example 23: the book prints 4900.3^{98} in the expansion and (4900)3^{97} in the bracketed line. The coefficient is \binom{100}{2} = \frac{100 \times 99}{2} = 4950. The remainder 1 is not affected. (The book also prints "intiger" for integer.)
Book correction: Example 24(ii): the question is (25)^{272} but the solution writes (25)^{271}. Any power of 25 ends in 5, so the answer 5 is right either way.

Book correction: Example 25: the question prints the number as \frac{2}{31}; the solution works with \frac{2^{504}}{31}, which is the intended number (\frac{2}{31} itself is less than 1, so its fractional part would simply be \frac{2}{31}). The solution also says "8h is an integer"; the integer part found is 16h. The answer k = 16 is right.
Book correction: Example 26: the book prints "A multiple of 100 + 6(120) + 1 = 100k + 72". Since 6(120) + 1 = 721, it should read 100k + 21. The stated last two digits, 21, are right.

Book correction: Example 27: in the last two lines of working the book keeps a "+ \dots + 1 +" inside the expansions and inside the bracket after 14. The +1 from (14 + 1)^{13} and the -1 from (14 - 1)^{15} cancel, so no 1 remains; the first group should end with {}^{13}C_{12}(14), and with {}^{13}C_{12} after 14 is taken out. The conclusion is right.
